hypotheses.title: Loss of airflow at CT-401 Cooling Tower (fan failure)
hypotheses.mechanism: Without forced draught the tower rejects far less heat. Basin temperature climbs, the trim chiller loads up until it saturates, and warmer cooling water then reaches the process.

criteria.description: Fan reports a trip, or fan current / vibration has collapsed
criteria.detail: CT-401.FAN_CURRENT low (5.80 A, baseline 38.0); CT-401.FAN_VIB low (0.43 mm/s, baseline 2.40)

criteria.description: Basin water temperature is high or rising
Downstream chiller is loading up
criteria.detail: CH-402.LOAD high (100 %, baseline 25.2); CH-402.COMP_CURRENT high (151 A, baseline 69.2)

criteria.description: Cooling-water supply temperature is high or rising
Process cooler outlet temperature is high or rising

unknowns: Ambient wet-bulb temperature is not measured, so a weather-driven rise cannot be excluded by the engine.
hypotheses.verification: Local inspection of the fan drive: starter trip flag, gearbox, blades.

hypotheses.title: High-resistance connection at the MCC-510 Motor Control Centre A incomer
hypotheses.mechanism: A deteriorating bolted joint or contact adds series resistance: voltage is lost across it and dissipated as heat at the joint. Constant-power loads downstream draw more current to compensate.

criteria.description: Bus voltage at this board is low
Incomer joint temperature is high or rising
Two or more consumers fed from this board draw more current
criteria.detail: Not detected on M-101.CURRENT, M-102.CURRENT, M-401.CURRENT

criteria.description: Voltage at the transformer and at the neighbouring board is normal (the drop is local to this board)
criteria.detail: TX-501.LV_VOLT 398 V (0.1σ from baseline); MCC-520.VOLT 398 V (-0.6σ from baseline)

criteria.description: Voltage is also low at the transformer terminals (an upstream cause)
Bus voltage at this board is within its baseline (no voltage is being lost across the joint)

unknowns: No thermal imaging or per-phase voltages; the joint temperature is a single-point measurement.
hypotheses.verification: Thermographic survey of the incomer and a micro-ohm test of the joint, with the board made safe.

hypotheses.title: Capacity fault in CH-402 Trim Chiller
hypotheses.mechanism: A chiller that trips or unloads stops trimming the supply temperature; cooling water leaves it warmer while the chiller itself draws little power.

criteria.description: Cooling-water supply temperature is high or rising
Chiller load or compressor current has dropped
Chiller is running at high load (it is responding, not failing)
criteria.detail: CH-402.LOAD high (100 %, baseline 25.2); CH-402.COMP_CURRENT high (151 A, baseline 69.2)

criteria.description: Water arriving from the tower is already too warm

unknowns: Refrigerant-side pressures and the chiller alarm log are not available to the engine.
hypotheses.verification: Chiller controller alarm history and refrigerant circuit readings.
